subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Prestressed Concrete: Squeezing for Strength
description: Learn Prestressed Concrete: Squeezing for Strength in one minute.

hook.text: You can make a row of books act like a beam by squeezing them tightly between your hands.

buildup.text: Prestressed concrete uses tensioned steel cables inside the concrete. They squeeze it before any load is applied.

discovery.text: Pre-compression cancels out the tension that loads create. The concrete never experiences pulling forces.

twist.text: Eugène Freyssinet invented it in 1928, but nobody cared until steel shortages after WWII made efficiency essential.

climax.text: Prestressed concrete enables longer bridge spans, thinner floors, and lighter structures than regular reinforced concrete.

punchline.text: Squeeze concrete before loading it. It'll never crack.

quiz.question: How does prestressing improve concrete's performance?
options: It heats the concrete to increase its density permanently
Pre-compression cancels the tension that loads would create
It adds air bubbles that absorb shock from heavy loads
